mainTopic: Whether a bird's שחיטה is from the Torah, and whether cutting only the windpipe is enough for a bird.
overview: The גמרא finishes testing the claim of רבי יצחק בן פנחס that a bird has no Torah requirement of שחיטה. A proof from a ברייתא about covering blood is pushed off by saying the case is a חיה. A משנה about מליקה done with a knife does seem to require Torah שחיטה for birds. The גמרא answers that רבי יצחק בן פנחס follows רבי אלעזר הקפר, who learns from a פסוק that a צבי and an איל need שחיטה but a bird needs it only מדברי סופרים. רבי disagrees and learns the rules of שחיטה, including cutting most of one סימן in a bird, from 'כאשר צויתך'. Then רב נחמן and רב אדא בר אהבה argue whether that one סימן can be either pipe or must be the ושט. Several sources are brought on each side and pushed off, until a ברייתא on מליקה of a חטאת העוף refutes רב אדא בר אהבה. The גמרא then wonders whether מליקה is different from regular שחיטה. It begins a story about a duck in רבא's house to settle the question, and the story continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Trying to read the ברייתא as talking about a bird
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the ברייתא just quoted, about covering blood, is talking about a bird whose blood someone wants for removing moths. If so, it would show that birds need שחיטה by Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't the ברייתא talking about a bird, where the person wants its blood to get rid of a moth?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is trying to prove from the earlier ברייתא that birds need שחיטה by Torah law. It does this by suggesting the case is about a bird.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier ברייתא treats a stabbed or improperly killed animal differently from a properly slaughtered one when it comes to covering the blood. If that rule applies to a bird, then a bird must have a real Torah שחיטה. Otherwise stabbing it would count just like slaughtering it, and its blood would also need covering.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it? A way of proposing how to read a source
Bird
A moth (people used blood to treat clothing against it)

phrases.english: What, is it not about a bird,
phrases.notes: This refers back to the ברייתא quoted just before this, about covering the blood when someone needs the blood.

phrases.english: where he needs its blood for a moth?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the attempt, begun before this text, to prove from a ברייתא about covering blood that birds need שחיטה by Torah law.
steps.raayaObject: That שחיטה of a bird is required by Torah law, against רבי יצחק בן פנחס.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The earlier ברייתא about covering blood, read as a case of a bird whose blood is used against moths.

steps.title: No, the ברייתא is talking about a wild animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The ברייתא is about a חיה whose blood is wanted as red dye, not about a bird.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It is talking about a wild animal, where he wants its blood for dye.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof by reading the ברייתא as a case of a חיה, not a bird.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees that a חיה needs שחיטה by Torah law. If the ברייתא is about a חיה, it tells us nothing about birds, so the view of רבי יצחק בן פנחס still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: A wild (undomesticated) kosher animal, like a deer
Red dye

phrases.english: No, it is about a wild animal,
where he needs its blood for dye.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 1 by changing the case from a bird to a חיה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the reading of the ברייתא as being about a bird.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא can be about a חיה, which needs שחיטה anyway, so nothing is proven about birds.

steps.title: Proof from מליקה done with a knife
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says that if a bird offering's neck was cut from behind with a knife, the bird is a נבילה and makes clothes impure when swallowed. If birds needed no Torah שחיטה, the knife cutting the סימנים should at least save it from being a נבילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If someone did מליקה with a knife, the bird makes clothes impure while it is in the throat. If birds have no Torah שחיטה, then even though breaking the spine and neck made it a טריפה, the knife should still save it from being a נבילה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new proof, from a משנה, that birds do need שחיטה by Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cutting with a knife from the back first breaks the spine and neck, which makes the bird a טריפה. Then the knife cuts the סימנים. If birds had no special Torah שחיטה, this knife cut should be good enough to keep the bird from being a נבילה. Since the משנה still calls it a נבילה that makes clothes impure, it seems a bird needs a proper Torah שחיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: Did מְלִיקָה, killing a bird offering by cutting the back of its neck with the fingernail
The throat. Meat of a kosher bird's נבילה makes clothes impure while it is being swallowed
The spine and the neck bone
An animal with a fatal defect. It is forbidden to eat but does not give off טומאה
An animal that died without valid שחיטה. It is forbidden and gives off טומאה

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up טריפה and נבילה. A טריפה is forbidden to eat but is not impure. A נבילה is impure. The question here is only why the bird is a נבילה.

phrases.english: Come and hear: If he cut the nape of the neck with a knife,
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in זבחים. Normally מליקה is done with the fingernail, not a knife.

phrases.english: it makes clothes impure while in the throat.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ אֵין שְׁחִיטָה לָעוֹף מִן הַתּוֹרָה,
phrases.english: And if you say a bird has no slaughter from the Torah,
granted that when he breaks
the spine and neck bone, it becomes a tereifa,

phrases.aramaic: תַּהְנֵי לַהּ סַכִּין לְטַהֲרָהּ מִידֵּי נְבֵלָה!
phrases.english: the knife should work to save it from being a neveila!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof failed, the גמרא brings a new and stronger proof from a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That שחיטה of a bird is required by Torah law.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in זבחים: מליקה done with a knife makes the bird a נבילה.

steps.title: רבי יצחק בן פנחס follows a different תנא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יצחק בן פנחס holds like a different תנא, רבי אלעזר הקפר. That תנא asks what we learn from the פסוק comparing to a צבי and an איל.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds like this תנא, as it is taught: רבי אלעזר הקפר ברבי says: Why does the פסוק say, "Just as the צבי is eaten"? What do we learn from the צבי and איל now?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא does not argue with the משנה. It says that רבי יצחק בן פנחס follows another תנא, and it starts quoting that תנא's ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof from the משנה is accepted as correct for that משנה. But a different תנא holds that birds have no Torah שחיטה, so רבי יצחק בן פנחס is not stuck without support. The ברייתא opens with a question: the פסוק compares פסולי המוקדשין to a צבי and an איל, but what does that comparison add?

keyTerms.meaning: Like this תנא, following the view of a particular Sage of the משנה period
Why does the פסוק need to say this?
Gazelle and deer, two kinds of חיה

phrases.aramaic: הוּא דְּאָמַר כִּי הַאי תַּנָּא, דְּתַנְיָא:
phrases.english: He says it like this tanna, as it is taught:
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי יצחק בן פנחס, the one who said birds have no Torah שחיטה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar HaKappar the distinguished Sage says:
What does the verse teach by saying
"However, as the gazelle is eaten, etc."?

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי מָה לָמַדְנוּ מִצְּבִי וְאַיָּל מֵעַתָּה?
phrases.english: And what have we learned from gazelle and deer up to now?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the proof of step 3 by saying the משנה is one view and רבי יצחק בן פנחס follows another תנא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Does not reject the משנה's meaning. It only rejects the idea that this משנה defeats רבי יצחק בן פנחס.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumes everyone agrees with that משנה, but there is a תנא who disagrees.

steps.title: צבי and איל need שחיטה, but a bird needs it only מדברי סופרים
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר הקפר answers that the comparison works both ways. Just as פסולי המוקדשין need שחיטה, so do a צבי and an איל. But a bird's שחיטה is only rabbinic.
steps.simpleTranslation: This came to teach and ended up being taught. The פסוק compares צבי and איל to פסולי המוקדשין: just as פסולי המוקדשין need שחיטה, so too צבי and איל need שחיטה. A bird has no שחיטה from the Torah, only from the Sages.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question and ends with the key line: a bird needs שחיטה only מדברי סופרים. This is the source for רבי יצחק בן פנחס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The צבי and איל were brought in to teach a law about פסולי המוקדשין. But we also learn something about the צבי and איל themselves: they need שחיטה, because פסולי המוקדשין need it. Since this comparison covers only animals like the צבי and איל, the Torah has no source requiring שחיטה for a bird.

keyTerms.meaning: Came to teach and ended up being taught. The example used to teach is itself taught something
Compares, making a הֶקֵּשׁ that links two things in a פסוק
Consecrated animals that became blemished and were redeemed, so they may now be eaten
From the words of the Sages, a rabbinic law

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אלעזר הקפר, which is the view רבי יצחק בן פנחס follows, a צבי and an איל need שחיטה by Torah law, but a bird needs שחיטה only מדברי סופרים. The משנה about מליקה with a knife follows a different view.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the question of whether a bird's שחיטה is from the Torah is a real argument between תנאים.

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי זֶה בָּא לְלַמֵּד וְנִמְצָא לָמֵד,
phrases.english: This came to teach and is found to be taught,
it compares gazelle and deer to disqualified consecrated animals:
just as disqualified consecrated animals need slaughter,
so too gazelle and deer need slaughter;

phrases.aramaic: וְעוֹף אֵין לוֹ שְׁחִיטָה מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
phrases.english: but a bird has no slaughter by Torah law,
only by rabbinic law.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי זֶה בָּא לְלַמֵּד וְנִמְצָא לָמֵד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question the ברייתא asked in step 4, and so gives the source that backs רבי יצחק בן פנחס.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The הקש teaches that a צבי and an איל need שחיטה like פסולי המוקדשין. A bird is not included, so its שחיטה is only rabbinic.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יצחק בן פנחס follows רבי אלעזר הקפר: a bird's שחיטה is מדברי סופרים.

steps.title: Who disagrees with רבי אלעזר הקפר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא argues with רבי אלעזר הקפר and holds that a bird's שחיטה is from the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the תנא that disagrees with רבי אלעזר הקפר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question to find the other side of the argument. It is setting up the next step, where it names that תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 5, רבי אלעזר הקפר said a bird's שחיטה is only rabbinic. The גמרא now wants to know which תנא holds the opposite: that a bird needs שחיטה by Torah law.

keyTerms.meaning: A sage from the time of the משנה
Disagrees with him

phrases.aramaic: מַאן תַּנָּא דִּפְלִיג עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר הַקַּפָּר?
phrases.english: Who is the tanna who disagrees with Rabbi Elazar HaKappar?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks for the opposing view to רבי אלעזר הקפר's position in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the תנא who holds that a bird's שחיטה is from the Torah.

steps.title: רבי learns the laws of שחיטה from 'as I have commanded you'
steps.stepSummary: The answer is רבי. He learns from 'וזבחת... כאשר צויתך' that משה was taught the rules of שחיטה, including cutting most of one סימן in a bird.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי. A ברייתא teaches that רבי says the פסוק 'And you shall slaughter... as I have commanded you' shows that משה was commanded about the gullet, the windpipe, cutting most of one סימן in a bird, and most of two in an animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי is the one who disagrees. A ברייתא shows that he counts a bird's שחיטה as part of what משה was taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah says 'as I have commanded you,' but it never spells out how to slaughter. So רבי says משה was given these details orally. Since the bird rule (most of one סימן) is on the list, a bird's שחיטה is from the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: The gullet (food pipe)
The windpipe
The majority (most of it)
'As I have commanded you': points to laws taught orally

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the source for the basic rules of how much must be cut in a bird and in an animal.

phrases.english: It is Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi],
as it is taught: Rabbi says:
"And you shall slaughter… as I have commanded you" –
teaches that Moshe was commanded
about the gullet and about the windpipe,
and about the majority of one [siman] in a bird,
and about the majority of two in an animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי holds a bird's שחיטה is from the Torah, learned from 'כאשר צויתך'.

steps.title: Which one סימן works for a bird?
steps.stepSummary: About the משנה's 'one in a bird': רב נחמן says either the gullet or the windpipe works. רב אדא בר אהבה says only the gullet.
steps.simpleTranslation: About 'one in a bird,' it was said: רב נחמן said either the gullet or the windpipe. רב אדא בר אהבה said the gullet, not the windpipe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic: an argument between two אמוראים about which סימן counts when a bird needs only one cut.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees one סימן is enough for a bird. The question is whether that one can be either pipe (רב נחמן) or must be the gullet (רב אדא בר אהבה).

keyTerms.meaning: One [סימן] in a bird
Either... or

phrases.english: About 'one in a bird,' it was stated:
phrases.notes: This goes back to the משנה's rule that cutting one סימן in a bird is enough.

phrases.aramaic: רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר: אוֹ וֶושֶׁט אוֹ קָנֶה,
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: either the gullet or the windpipe,

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה אָמַר: וֶושֶׁט וְלֹא קָנֶה.
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said: the gullet and not the windpipe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new topic in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב נחמן: either סימן works for a bird. רב אדא בר אהבה: only the וושט.

steps.title: How each reads the word 'one'
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן reads 'one' as any one. רב אדא בר אהבה reads 'one' as 'the special one,' meaning the gullet.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן: the משנה says 'one,' and 'one' means any one. רב אדא בר אהבה: what does 'one' mean? The special one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats each opinion and explains how each fits the word 'one' in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides read the same word. רב נחמן takes 'אחד' plainly, as any one. רב אדא בר אהבה reads it as 'מיוחד,' the special or main one, which he says is the gullet.

keyTerms.meaning: Any at all, whichever
Special, the main one

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רב אדא בר אהבה changes the משנה's word. He keeps 'one' but understands it as 'the special one.'

phrases.aramaic: רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר: אוֹ וֶושֶׁט אוֹ קָנֶה –
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: either the gullet or the windpipe –
'one' is taught,
'one' means any one.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה אָמַר: וֶושֶׁט וְלֹא קָנֶה –
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said: the gullet and not the windpipe –
What is 'one'? The special one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how each opinion in step 8 fits the משנה's wording.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'אחד' = any one (רב נחמן); 'אחד' = מיוחד, the gullet (רב אדא בר אהבה).

steps.title: A memory aid for the coming challenges
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a list of key words to help remember the five sources it will bring.
steps.simpleTranslation: Memory aid: slaughtered, halves, windpipe, a nick, of a bird חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא gives a short list of words, one for each source it is about to bring in this argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word points to one coming source. 'Slaughtered' is the first one, which comes right after this. The list just helps the learner keep the order straight.

keyTerms.meaning: Memory aid (here, not a pipe)
Halves
A nick or flaw
A bird sin offering

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'סימן' means a memory aid. It is not the 'סימנים' (the two pipes) that are cut in שחיטה.

phrases.english: (Mnemonic: slaughtered, halves,
windpipe, nick, of a bird sin offering.)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Prepares for the list of challenges about the dispute in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A list of words to remember the coming sources.

steps.title: A ברייתא that mentions only cutting the gullet
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא talks about cutting the gullet when the windpipe slipped out of place, and never mentions cutting the windpipe. This seems to go against רב נחמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: A challenge: if he cut the gullet and then the windpipe slipped out of place, it is kosher. If the windpipe slipped first and then he cut the gullet, it is not valid. If he cut the gullet and found the windpipe slipped, and he does not know if it slipped before or after, this really happened, and they said: any doubt in שחיטה is not valid. But cutting the windpipe is not taught.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב נחמן. The ברייתא only talks about cutting the gullet, which suggests cutting the windpipe would not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא builds all its cases around cutting the וושט. If cutting the קנה were just as good, as רב נחמן says, the ברייתא could have taught the same cases with the קנה. Leaving it out suggests only the gullet works, like רב אדא בר אהבה.

keyTerms.meaning: The windpipe (another name for the קנה)
Slipped out of place
Valid / not valid
A doubt about the slaughter
Whereas, but

phrases.english: They raised an objection: If he cut the gullet
and afterward the windpipe slipped out of place – it is valid,

phrases.aramaic: נִשְׁמְטָה הַגַּרְגֶּרֶת וְאַחַר כָּךְ שָׁחַט אֶת הַוֶּושֶׁט – פְּסוּלָה,
phrases.english: if the windpipe slipped out of place and afterward he cut the gullet – it is not valid,

phrases.aramaic: שָׁחַט אֶת הַוֶּושֶׁט וְנִמְצֵאת גַּרְגֶּרֶת שְׁמוּטָה
phrases.english: if he cut the gullet and the windpipe was found slipped out of place

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ אִם קוֹדֶם שְׁחִיטָה נִשְׁמְטָה
phrases.english: and he does not know whether it slipped before the slaughter
or whether it slipped after the slaughter –
this was an actual case, and they said:
any doubt in slaughter – it is not valid,
but slaughter of the windpipe is not taught.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The first source from the memory aid ('שחט'), brought against רב נחמן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's view that cutting either the וושט or the קנה is enough for a bird.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא teaches its cases only with cutting the וושט and leaves out cutting the קנה, suggesting the קנה alone does not work.

steps.title: The windpipe was mentioned only because it tends to slip
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא spoke about a windpipe that slipped only because that is what usually happens. It does not mean that cutting the windpipe is not enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the windpipe tends to slip out of place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 11. The ברייתא described a windpipe that slipped and a cut ושט only because that is the common real-life case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 said the ברייתא never mentions cutting the גרגרת, so maybe only the ושט works. The answer is that the גרגרת is the one that usually slips, so the ברייתא described the normal case. This tells us nothing about whether cutting the גרגרת alone is valid, so רב נחמן is safe.

keyTerms.meaning: It tends to slip out of place

phrases.english: Because the windpipe tends to slip out of place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back the challenge against רב נחמן raised in Step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the ברייתא's silence about cutting the windpipe
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא described the common case of a slipping windpipe. It was not making a rule that only the ושט works.

steps.title: רבי יהודה mentions only the gullet for a bird
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says cutting half of each סימן in a bird is not valid. רבי יהודה adds that a bird needs the ושט and the veins cut, and he says nothing about the windpipe. This seems to go against רב נחמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If someone cut two halves of the סימנים in a bird, it is not valid, and certainly not in an animal. רבי יהודה says: in a bird, it is not valid until he cuts the gullet and the veins.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second source against רב נחמן. רבי יהודה names only the ושט for a bird.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If either סימן worked, רבי יהודה could have said 'the gullet or the windpipe.' He mentioned only the ושט, which sounds like רב אדא בר אהבה's view that only the gullet works.

keyTerms.meaning: Half of each of the two סימנים
Invalid (the שחיטה does not work)
It goes without saying
The main blood vessels of the neck

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע: שָׁחַט שְׁנֵי חֲצָאֵי סִימָנִין בְּעוֹף
phrases.english: Come and hear: If one cut two halves of the simanim in a bird
it is invalid, and needless to say in an animal.
Rabbi Yehuda says: In a bird,

phrases.aramaic: – עַד שֶׁיִּשְׁחוֹט אֶת הַוֶּושֶׁט וְאֶת הַוְּרִידִין,
phrases.english: it is not valid until he cuts the gullet and the veins.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: שָׁחַט שְׁנֵי חֲצָאֵי סִימָנִין בְּעוֹף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the second of the sources listed in Step 10, after the first one was pushed back.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's view that either סימן works for a bird
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה names only the ושט for a bird. If the windpipe also worked, he should have mentioned it.

steps.title: The gullet is mentioned because it sits next to the veins
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה mentioned the ושט only because it lies next to the veins, which he wants cut. It does not mean the windpipe cannot work.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the gullet is next to the veins.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back the challenge. רבי יהודה named the gullet only because it is near the veins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's real point is that the veins must be cut. Since the ושט is right beside them, cutting there naturally reaches the veins, so he mentioned the ושט. This does not rule out cutting the windpipe, so רב נחמן still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: The gullet (food pipe)
Next to, nearby

phrases.english: Because the gullet is adjacent to the veins.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back the challenge from רבי יהודה in Step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from רבי יהודה naming only the ושט
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: He named the ושט because of where it sits next to the veins. He was not saying it is the only valid סימן.

steps.title: Finishing half a windpipe after a pause seems to support רב נחמן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that if someone cut half the windpipe, paused, and then finished, the שחיטה is valid. The גמרא suggests this is a bird and that he finished the windpipe, which would show the windpipe alone works.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If someone cut half the windpipe, paused for as long as it takes to do another שחיטה, and then finished his שחיטה, it is valid. Isn't this talking about a bird, and doesn't 'finished it' mean he finished the windpipe?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא switches direction and tries to prove רב נחמן right from a ברייתא about a cut windpipe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא mentions only the windpipe and says the שחיטה is valid once it is 'finished.' If this is a bird and 'finished' means he finished the windpipe, then cutting the windpipe alone is enough. That is exactly רב נחמן's view.

keyTerms.meaning: He paused for as long as it takes to slaughter another animal
He finished it

phrases.english: Come and hear: If one cut half the windpipe,
and paused for the length of another slaughter,
and then completed his slaughter, it is valid.
Is it not talking about a bird,
and what does 'completed it' mean? He completed the windpipe?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: שָׁחַט חֲצִי גַרְגֶּרֶת, וְשָׁהָה כְּדֵי שְׁחִיטָה אַחֶרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רב נחמן twice, the גמרא now tries to prove him right.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן's view that the windpipe alone works for a bird
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about finishing a half-cut windpipe after a pause, read as a bird where only the windpipe was finished

steps.title: It could be an animal where he finished the whole שחיטה
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed back. The ברייתא may be about a בהמה, and 'finished' may mean he finished the whole שחיטה, both סימנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is talking about an animal, and 'finished it' means he finished the whole שחיטה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof for רב נחמן by reading the ברייתא as talking about an animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the case is a בהמה, both סימנים must be cut anyway. Then 'finished' means he went on to cut both, so the ברייתא says nothing about a bird using only the windpipe. The proof for רב נחמן falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: No (the גמרא rejecting a suggested reading)
A domesticated animal, which needs both סימנים cut
The entire שחיטה

phrases.english: No, it is talking about an animal,
and what does 'completed it' mean? He completed the entire slaughter.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, בִּבְהֵמָה, וּמַאי גְּמָרָהּ – גְּמָרָהּ לִשְׁחִיטָה כּוּלַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof for רב נחמן from Step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reading that the case is a bird and only the windpipe was finished
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא can be read as an animal where the whole שחיטה was finished, so it does not show the windpipe alone works.

steps.title: Finishing a half-damaged windpipe seems to support רב נחמן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that if half the windpipe was already damaged, and the שוחט added any amount and finished, the שחיטה is valid. The גמרא suggests this is a bird and that he finished the windpipe.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If half the windpipe was damaged, and he added any amount to it and finished it, his שחיטה is valid. Isn't this a bird, and doesn't 'finished it' mean he finished the windpipe?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries another proof for רב נחמן, from a ברייתא about a windpipe that was already half damaged.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again only the windpipe is mentioned, and the שחיטה is called valid. If it is a bird and 'finished' means finishing the windpipe, then the windpipe alone is enough, just as רב נחמן says.

keyTerms.meaning: The windpipe (same as גַּרְגֶּרֶת)
Damaged, already partly cut
Any amount at all, even a tiny bit

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע: הֲרֵי שֶׁהָיָה חֲצִי קָנֶה פָּגוּם,
phrases.english: Come and hear: If half the windpipe was damaged,
and he added to it any amount and completed it,
his slaughter is valid.
Is it not talking about a bird,
and what does 'completed it' mean? He completed the windpipe?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: הֲרֵי שֶׁהָיָה חֲצִי קָנֶה פָּגוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second attempt to prove רב נחמן right, built the same way as Step 15.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן's view that the windpipe alone works for a bird
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about a half-damaged windpipe that was finished, read as a bird

steps.title: It could be an animal where he finished by cutting the gullet
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed back. The ברייתא may be about a בהמה, and 'finished' means he finished by cutting the ושט too.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is talking about an animal, and 'finished it' means he finished by cutting the gullet.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects this proof the same way as before, by reading the case as an animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a בהמה, the damaged half plus a little more gives a majority of the windpipe. 'Finished' then means he went on to cut the ושט, so both סימנים were cut. Nothing here proves a bird can use the windpipe alone. The next step brings a stronger source, which the גמרא treats as a refutation of רב אדא בר אהבה.

keyTerms.meaning: He finished it
By cutting the gullet

steps.whatToRemember: Every source brought so far can be read either way. Mentioning only one סימן may just describe the usual case or the cut needed in an animal, so none of them decides between רב נחמן and רב אדא בר אהבה yet.

phrases.english: No, it is talking about an animal,
and what does 'completed it' mean? He completed it with the gullet.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, בִּבְהֵמָה, וּמַאי גְּמָרוֹ – גְּמָרוֹ לְוֶושֶׁט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof for רב נחמן from Step 17.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reading that the case is a bird and only the windpipe was finished
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא can be an animal where 'finished' means cutting the ושט as well, so both סימנים were cut.

steps.title: Proof from how a bird sin offering is pinched
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that in מליקה of a חטאת העוף the כהן cuts one סימן, either the ושט or the קנה. This suggests the קנה alone is enough for a bird.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: How is a bird sin offering pinched? He cuts the spine and the neck bone without cutting most of the flesh, until he reaches the gullet or the windpipe. Once he reaches the gullet or the windpipe, he cuts one סימן and most of the flesh with it. For a bird burnt offering, he cuts both סימנים or most of both.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about מליקה to prove that cutting only the windpipe works for a bird.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the כהן reaches 'the ושט or the קנה' and cuts one סימן, so either one is enough. If the קנה alone works for a חטאת העוף, it seems a bird does not need its ושט cut. Unlike the earlier proofs, this one cannot be pushed off as being about a בהמה, because מליקה is only done to birds.

keyTerms.meaning: The כהן cutting a bird קרבן's neck from the back with his thumbnail, instead of שחיטה
A bird brought as a sin offering
A bird brought as a burnt offering
The spine and the neck bone
One of the two pipes in the neck that must be cut, the קנה or the ושט

steps.whyThisMatters: The earlier proofs (steps 15-18) failed because the ברייתות could have been about a בהמה. A ברייתא about מליקה has to be about a bird, so this proof is much stronger.

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע: כֵּיצַד מוֹלְקִין חַטַּאת הָעוֹף?
phrases.english: Come and hear: How does one pinch a bird sin offering?
He cuts the spine and the neck bone
without cutting most of the flesh
until he reaches the gullet or the windpipe;
once he has reached the gullet or the windpipe,

phrases.aramaic: חוֹתֵךְ סִימָן אֶחָד וְרוֹב בָּשָׂר עִמּוֹ,
phrases.english: he cuts one סימן and most of the flesh along with it,
and with a burnt offering, he cuts two, or most of two.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: כֵּיצַד מוֹלְקִין חַטַּאת הָעוֹף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new and stronger proof, after the proofs in steps 15 and 17 were pushed back
steps.raayaObject: That in a bird, cutting only the קנה is enough
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on מליקה: 'he cuts one סימן', meaning either the ושט or the קנה

steps.title: רב אדא בר אהבה is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא declares that the ברייתא on מליקה is a full refutation of רב אדא בר אהבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The refutation of רב אדא בר אהבה is a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that רב אדא בר אהבה, who held a bird needs its ושט cut, is disproven by this ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since מליקה is only for birds and the ברייתא lets the קנה alone count, the view that a bird must have its ושט cut seems impossible to defend. A double 'תיובתא' is the גמרא's way of saying the refutation is final.

keyTerms.meaning: A refutation that disproves an אמורא's opinion

steps.whatToRemember: At this point רב אדא בר אהבה is formally refuted: in מליקה, one סימן, even just the קנה, is enough.

phrases.aramaic: תְּיוּבְתָּא דְּרַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה, תְּיוּבְתָּא.
phrases.english: The refutation of רב אדא בר אהבה is a refutation.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּיוּבְתָּא דְּרַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה, תְּיוּבְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: States the result of the proof in step 19
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב אדא בר אהבה's view, that a bird needs its ושט cut, is refuted

steps.title: What is the final ruling?
steps.stepSummary: Someone asks what the final הלכה is on whether the windpipe alone works for a bird.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was concluded about it?
steps.whatsHappening: A question is raised: what is the bottom line on this issue? This sets up the next two moves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even after a תיובתא, the questioner wants to know the practical הלכה. Step 23 shows why he is not yet satisfied.

keyTerms.meaning: What was decided about it, meaning what is the final הלכה

phrases.english: What was concluded about it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical הלכה after the refutation
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The final הלכה on whether cutting only the קנה is valid for a bird

steps.title: It is just as you said
steps.stepSummary: The reply expresses surprise at the question: the matter is clear, it was refuted just as stated.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'What was concluded about it?!' It is as you said.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer repeats the question in surprise and says the issue is already settled: רב אדא בר אהבה was refuted, as was just said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The responder thinks the תיובתא already decides the halacha, so the question seems unnecessary to him. This sets up the questioner's explanation of his doubt in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: As you said

phrases.english: 'What was concluded about it?!' It is as you said,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 21 by pointing back to the תיובתא of step 20
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The refutation of רב אדא בר אהבה stands, so the windpipe alone works

steps.title: Maybe pinching is different
steps.stepSummary: The questioner explains his doubt: מליקה may be different, because the spine and neck bone are also cut, so the proof may not carry over to regular שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps it is different there, because there the spine and neck bone are cut.
steps.whatsHappening: The proof from מליקה is weakened. Cutting the קנה may be enough there only because so much else, the spine and neck bone, is cut too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In מליקה the bird's spine and neck bone are cut before the כהן reaches the סימנים. That extra cutting may be why one סימן, even the קנה, is enough. Ordinary שחיטה has no such extra cut, so there the ושט may still be needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps it is different there, used to say a proof does not carry over

steps.confusionAlert: This does not bring back רב אדא בר אהבה's view as the הלכה. It only shows the ברייתא may not prove what happens in regular שחיטה. Steps 24-25 begin a new attempt to settle that, using a case from רבא's house.

phrases.english: perhaps it is different there,
phrases.notes: 'There' means מליקה, the case in the ברייתא.

phrases.english: since there the spine and neck bone are cut.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּלְמָא שָׁאנֵי הָתָם, דְּאִיכָּא שִׁדְרָה וּמַפְרֶקֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the questioner in step 21 was unsure despite the refutation
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Limits the proof of step 19 to מליקה, not ordinary שחיטה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In מליקה the spine and neck bone are also cut, which may be why one סימן is enough

steps.title: So what is the הלכה for regular slaughter?
steps.stepSummary: With the proof weakened, the גמרא asks again what the הלכה is for שחיטה of a bird.
steps.simpleTranslation: What then?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks again what the הלכה is for ordinary שחיטה of a bird, since the מליקה proof may not apply. This sets up the story that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 23 left it unclear whether the קנה alone works in שחיטה. This short question reopens the issue so a new source can settle it.

phrases.english: What then?
phrases.notes: He means: so what is the הלכה for regular שחיטה of a bird?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reopens the question after the doubt in step 23
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether, in ordinary שחיטה of a bird, cutting only the קנה is enough

steps.title: The duck in רבא's house
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a story: a duck in רבא's house had its neck smeared with blood, and רבא asked what to do with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: a certain duck was in רבא's house, and it came with its neck smeared with blood. רבא said: What should we do?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts telling a real case from רבא's house to answer the question. This step only sets up the story; רבא's solution comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The blood on the neck raised a worry that a סימן had been damaged, which could make the duck a טרפה. רבא's question 'what should we do?' prepares the move he makes next, which will show how he treated the סימנים of a bird.

keyTerms.meaning: A duck
Its neck was smeared with blood
What should we do?

phrases.english: Come and hear: a certain duck
that was in רבא's house,
came with its neck smeared with blood.
רבא said: What should we do?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: דְּהָהוּא בַּר אֲוָוזָא דַּהֲוָה בֵּי רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new proof to answer the question of step 24
steps.raayaObject: The הלכה for cutting the סימנים in ordinary שחיטה of a bird
steps.raayaSupportSource: A real case of a duck brought to רבא
